critical_code_review_comments: device_binding.py:324 — OTP generation uses str(uuid.uuid4().int)[-1] repeated 6x. Each iteration recomputes a fresh UUID, so the OTP is effectively random, but the pattern is unusual. Consider `''.join(secrets.choice(string.digits) for _ in range(6))` for clarity + cryptographic randomness.
device_binding.py:107 NATIVE_DEVICE_ID_PATTERN — regex does not enforce a MAX length; a 500-char device_id would pass {6,}. Consider bounding to {6,128} to defend against DB bloat.

auth.py:181 signup_device_id = data.get('device_id') or data.get('device_fingerprint') — falls back to device_fingerprint if device_id absent. Since fingerprints don't match the AND-/IOS- pattern they never trigger enforcement (safe by Q2=a); just documenting the fallback.

Admin endpoints require both X-Admin-Pin PIN AND JWT bearer (global auth middleware). AdminDeviceBinding.js headers() only sets 'X-Admin-Pin' — it relies on axios default interceptor injecting Authorization from localStorage. Curl tests need both headers.

device_binding.py:487 admin_set_flag clears the local module cache (_clear_flag_cache) but does NOT propagate to other worker processes if uvicorn scales beyond 1 worker. The 5-min TTL will resolve eventually. Consider pub/sub or redis-backed flag if going multi-worker.
